modifications: Entries were selected, normalised (HTML removed, years parsed, headline titles shortened to about 100 characters with an ellipsis), merged and de-duplicated across sources, ranked, capped per day and category, and sorted. Summaries keep the source wording. did_you_know facts are either Wikipedia "Did you know" hooks (text only, reformatted) or one-sentence rewordings of existing entries (prefixed with the date, possibly shortened). Image links are unmodified Wikimedia URLs.

did_you_know.fact: On December 3, 1992: A test engineer for Sema Group uses a personal computer to send the world's first text message via the Vodafone network to the phone of a colleague.
On December 3, 1973: Pioneer program: Pioneer 10 sends back the first close-up images of Jupiter.
On December 3, 1929: President Herbert Hoover delivers his first State of the Union message to Congress. It is presented in the form of a written message rather than a speech.
On December 3, 1910: Modern neon lighting is first demonstrated by Georges Claude at the Paris Motor Show.

On December 3, 1898: The Duquesne Country and Athletic Club defeats an all-star collection of early football players 16–0, in what is considered to be the first all-star game for professional American football.
